steps.name: QC and batch/condition structure check
caveats: counts.csv is 12000 x 13 but metadata.csv is 12 x 3 — verify sample name overlap between the two files and reconcile which 12 (or 13) samples enter the model before proceeding; report the discrepancy explicitly rather than silently dropping/adding a sample
Do not batch-correct the counts themselves for visualization purposes beyond variance stabilization — keep raw batch effect visible in PCA to confirm the balanced design
steps.question: Do library sizes, PCA, and sample clustering confirm the annotated 6-treated-vs-6-control design with two balanced processing batches, and are there any sample outliers or mislabeling flags before differential expression?
acceptance_criteria: Library size (total counts) reported per sample from counts.csv
PCA (or similar ordination) computed on variance-stabilized/log-normalized counts, plotted colored by condition and by batch
Sample-metadata cross-check confirms which samples are treated/control and which batch each belongs to, and flags any count-matrix vs metadata sample-name mismatches
Any outlier sample noted with justification, without being removed unless clearly technical failure

steps.name: Differential expression, treated vs control, batch-adjusted
caveats: With only 2 batches and 6 samples per condition, the batch term consumes one degree of freedom per extra batch level — confirm this does not leave too few residual df; report actual residual df used
Use the metadata's batch and condition columns exactly as given — do not re-derive or infer batch assignment
If a sample count mismatch was found in T1S1, resolve it here consistently with what was decided upstream and state the final n used
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control kidney samples when adjusting for the two known, condition-balanced processing batches (design ~ batch + condition)?
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 run on raw integer counts with design formula ~ batch + condition, condition releveled so control is reference
Results table with log2FoldChange, shrunken LFC (apeglm or ashr), p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value for every gene, sorted by adjusted p-value
Number of genes significant at padj < 0.05 (and a note on |log2FC| threshold used, e.g. 1) reported explicitly
Independent filtering / dispersion diagnostics (dispersion plot) reported to confirm model fit is reasonable given n=6 per group

steps.name: Volcano and heatmap visualization of DE results
caveats: Heatmap should show that within-condition batch variation is smaller than between-condition variation for the top DE genes, corroborating the batch-adjusted model; note if it does not
steps.question: What do the top differentially expressed genes between treated and control kidney samples look like, and how do they separate the two groups?
acceptance_criteria: Volcano plot (log2FC vs -log10 padj) generated from the T1S2 results table with significance thresholds marked
Heatmap of top ~30-50 DE genes (by padj) across all 12/13 samples, annotated by condition and batch, using variance-stabilized counts
Plots saved as output files referencing actual gene symbols from counts.csv

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of DE genes
caveats: Gene identifiers in counts.csv are gene symbols and WikiPathways human GMT member genes are HGNC symbols — confirm the join before reporting a null/empty enrichment result as biological rather than an ID-mismatch artifact
steps.question: Which WikiPathways pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control kidney samples?
acceptance_criteria: Over-representation analysis (or ranked GSEA using the full DE stat) run against the human WikiPathways gene sets available in the environment

Enrichment run separately (or with sign-aware ranking) for up- and down-regulated genes if using ORA, or a single signed ranked-list GSEA reported with normalized enrichment scores and adjusted p-values
Pathway names reported human-readably (parsed from the '%'-delimited GMT descriptor) rather than raw IDs
If the WikiPathways human reference is unavailable at run time, the step reports that explicitly rather than fabricating enrichment results

plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch adjustment
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq of human kidney tissue with 12000 genes x 13 samples (note: metadata lists 12 samples with condition and batch — 6 treated vs 6 control, balanced across two known processing batches). Raw salmon-derived integer counts and a clean sample table make DESeq2 with an additive batch term the natural first step: the balanced 3x2 design lets a ~condition + batch model cleanly separate the batch effect from the treatment effect without confounding. QC (library size, PCA colored by batch and condition) comes first to confirm the batch structure looks as described and to catch any sample-metadata mismatch before fitting. Differential expression follows with the batch-adjusted model, then results are visualized (volcano, heatmap of top hits) and pushed to WikiPathways enrichment (human GMT reference available) to give the DE gene list biological context. Because two known batches are already annotated as a design factor, no additional latent-factor correction (e.g., ComBat/SVA) is planned — that would be redundant with modeling batch directly in DESeq2 and could remove real biology if the batch estimate is noisy given the modest n=12.
